div.b: What the gateway holds, one of two
div.span:
API Key — a key from the Anthropic console.
Workload Identity Federation — no Anthropic
key is stored at all. The gateway presents a JWT
from your IdP and exchanges it for a short-lived
token. Cached for 15 minutes at most.

text.tspan: What the gateway holds, one of two

Workload Identity Federation — no Anthropic
key is stored at all. The gateway presents a JWT
from your IdP and exchanges it for a short-lived
token. Cached for 15 minutes at most.

div.div:
Basic information
Name, Short Description
Slug default-anthropic — what the app names in the call
Authentication Type two cards, not three
API Key or Workload Identity Federation. There is no OAuth
Client Credentials option on this tile, unlike Open AI.
Federation fields, when that type is selected
Token Endpoint, Client ID, Client Secret, Scope, Audience,
then Federation Rule ID, Organization ID, and the service
account the rule targets.
Model provisioning
All models, or an explicit allowlist. Everything off the list is
unreachable through this integration.
Workspace provisioning
Which teams see Anthropic in their Model Catalog, and each
team's budget and rate limit.

div.div:
Both live on the Anthropic side, and both fail with the same unhelpful
message: the subject token was rejected.
• Max JWT lifetime must be 5400 or higher when the identity
provider is Entra ID, because Entra tokens last up to 90 minutes.
The default of 3600 is too short and rejects a valid token.
• JTI replay protection must be disabled for Okta issuers. The
gateway reuses its cached IdP token while it is still valid, and Okta
tokens carry a jti, so the second exchange is read as a replay.
Entra tokens have no jti, so this does not apply there.
The gateway returns only the standard OAuth error code. The real
reason stays in gateway logs and never reaches the caller, so a
consultant debugging this from the client side is working blind.

div.div:
Claude.ai in a browser, the desktop app, and the mobile app have no
base URL setting. Nothing points them at a gateway, so that traffic
never reaches Observability and no budget, allowlist, or guardrail
touches it.
When a customer says "we use Claude", establish which one:
• Code calling api.anthropic.com — an SDK, an agent
framework, Claude Code, a CI job. This is what the gateway covers.
• People typing into claude.ai — covered by network egress
policy, a CASB or SASE control, or the plan's own admin tooling.
Not by the AI Gateway.

div.div:
1. Anthropic bills your Anthropic account for inference.
Unchanged by the gateway. Same rates, same console.
2. Palo Alto Networks meters flex credits by token volume.
1 token = 4 characters. Prompts, MCP, and agent-to-agent traffic
all count. Identical pricing for SaaS and Hybrid.
Because every call now carries one credential, the Anthropic side
collapses to a single principal. Per-team and per-app breakdown
moves into the gateway logs.
